https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri: The plugin catalog for this repository's integrations: visibility flags and card copy per entry. The data-browser fetches this file at runtime from GitHub Pages (https://ontola.github.io/atomic-plugins/integrations/catalog.json by default, configurable in Settings > Integration), not from the connected server. At the pinned atomic-server it reads only `shortname`, `experimental`, `enabled` and `requires-api-plugins`, to decide whether to offer the 'Show experimental plugins' toggle; it renders no card from this file (see integrations/READINESS.md). Where `shortname` equals a package directory under integrations/ (money, notion, pets), the entry's `version` must equal that package's (integrations/README.md, 'Version and catalog entry'). Flip `experimental` to `false` once its package.json `atomicCertification.support` has left "experimental" — see integrations/README.md.

What this bundled integration's sync or import can actually do, shown on its Integrations page card.
How and when this bundled integration exchanges data, shown on its Integrations page card.
The supported scope and caveats, shown in the card's 'Supported scope' details.

https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri: Import bank transactions from MT940 and camt.053 statement exports, and read them as a ledger in the Money drive app.
https://atomicdata.dev/integrations/prop: The importer checks that each statement's opening balance, transactions and closing balance add up, previews which transactions are new or already imported with exact amounts, dates, references and the bank's own descriptions, and writes nothing until you apply the host's review. It writes a Bank transactions table and an Imported statements table (one row per statement, with its opening and closing balance). The Money app shows the Bank transactions table as a ledger per account and currency, with the latest closing balance from a stored statement, search, period and direction filters, your own category and note per transaction, and an import from inside the app through the same review.
Upload an MT940 or camt.053 statement when you need it, on the importer's Import tab or from the Money app. No bank token and no live bank connection; nothing runs in the background.

MT940 (up to 512 KB) and camt.053 XML (up to 5 MB) files only, up to 500 transactions per file. No CSV or PDF, no payment initiation or live bank sync; bank-specific formats may need additional support. Saving a category or note needs you to allow the app to edit the table. The Money app works only as a view of the importer's Bank transactions table: installed from Drive apps it gets an empty table of its own with no importer, and the importer's table does not offer it under Add view, so installing it from here does not yet give a working Money app. Declared, and tested with synthetic statement files only at this version.

https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri: Where this integration's source can be fetched from, for entries not bundled as a local package.json in this folder. Optional — omitted for integrations developed in this repo.

The version of this integration currently published in this repository, mirrored from its package.json (see integrations/README.md). Omitted for an entry with no local package.json, such as one reached through the generic LocalThought/Devonian bridge or fetched from pluginUrl. A host compares this against what an installation has pinned to offer an update.

What this plugin needs from the node, derived from its manifest and never written by hand: a sorted JSON array such as ["persistent-host", "plugin-routes:read-only", "public-origin", "wasm-sandbox"], with `plugin-routes:<level>`, `operator-listener:<name>` and `operator-sidecar:<name>` for the gated surfaces of docs/design/server-plugin-routes.md section 0. The same list the host puts on each /plugin-catalog entry (atomic-server#1732), so a client can compare it with the node's `hostFeatures` without parsing manifests. Required on the entry of a package whose manifest is version 3 or needs the plugin-routes feature; integrations/tooling/catalog-requires.mjs checks it and writes it.

URL of the built ES module for exactly this entry's `version`, which a host installs as a drive app's entry point. Distinct from `pluginUrl`, which links to source. For an app built in this repo it is `https://ontola.github.io/atomic-plugins/apps/<shortname>/<version>/ui.js`: `integrations/<shortname>/app/build.mjs`'s output, committed at `apps/<shortname>/<version>/ui.js` and served by GitHub Pages from `main`. A version file on `main` is never changed or deleted, so a changed build needs a new version. A relative URL resolves against this catalog's own URL. See integrations/README.md, 'Publishing a drive app'.

Subresource Integrity hash (`sha384-` plus base64) of the `app-module` bytes. A host refuses to install or update from a module that does not match. `integrations/tooling/apps.mjs check` keeps it equal to the committed module and to a fresh build.
What one row in the installed app's table is called, singular (for example 'Pet'). Optional; the app may rename it itself.
What the installed app's table and its rows are called, plural (for example 'Pets'). Optional; given together with `app-row-name`.
